description: standard_flags:manifest:check and a client's contract check share these semantics. Each case gives the committed manifest (the baseline the client was built against) and the current one, and today's date (UTC). `invalid`: a manifest a reader must refuse (`invalid` names which: committed or current); nothing else is expected. `stale`: the two documents differ as JSON values, compared structurally: object member order is ignored, array order is significant (the server task compares the file's text instead). `removed_wires`: every wire (audience + name) the committed manifest tells an audience, from a flag's audiences or a tombstone's serve block still served today (today <= until), that the current manifest neither exposes to that audience nor serves from a tombstone whose until is today or later. `type_changes`: every wire both manifests tell the same audience whose JSON type (a flag's type; a static wire's boolean or string value) differs, whether or not a static wire's until has passed. `audiences_made_private`: every audience public in the committed manifest, with at least one wire served today, that the current manifest lists as not public. Lists are sorted by audience, then wire. `status` is breaking when any list is non-empty, else stale when stale, else ok. Version 1 manifests are server-only.

cases.name: identical manifests are ok
a changed default is only stale
an added wire and an added flag are only stale
a min_client added to a flag is only stale
a dropped alias with no tombstone is a removed wire
a removed flag whose tombstone serves every wire is only stale
a removed flag whose tombstone serves only some wires
a deprecated wire dropped before its until date is a removed wire; one past it may go
until is inclusive: on the until date the wire is still owed
the day after until, the deprecated wire may go
a tombstone that stopped serving a wire doesn't cover it
a wire whose flag became a different kind changed type
a deprecated wire that now serves a string changed type
a wire moved to another flag of the same type is only stale
a wire moved to another audience is removed from the first
an audience made public is only stale
a public audience made private while it serves wires is breaking
a public audience whose only wire's window is over may be made private
a wire past its until that comes back with another type is still a type change
member order doesn't make a manifest stale; array order does
reordered wires make a manifest stale
a wire listed on both a flag and a tombstone makes the manifest invalid
a serve block without until makes the manifest invalid
an until that isn't a calendar date makes the manifest invalid
a manifest holding only a version is invalid, not empty
an audience whose public isn't true or false makes the manifest invalid
a remove_by that isn't a calendar date makes the manifest invalid
a serve block without until_clients makes the manifest invalid
removed wires and type changes are reported together
a version 1 committed manifest is read: stale, and its wires still checked
